claim: Lao Unicode must be analyzed structurally rather than as a flat character list
Lao consonant letters do not behave as Thai-style inherent-vowel carriers
Modern Lao uses middle/high/low consonant classes in tone determination
Vientiane tone descriptions vary in exact contour labels and some analyses
Russian practical transcription is a position-sensitive Cyrillic tradition associated with Morev/Moskalev/Plam and geographical-name practice
Russian practical transcription writes aspirated stops with х sequences such as кх/пх/тх
Russian practical transcription renders Lao h as х
Russian practical transcription renders Lao /ɯ/ as ы
Ukrainian rendering should be generated from Lao IPA and the canonical Ukrainian inventory rather than inherited from Russian orthography
Serbian official sources render Vientiane as Вијентијан
Bulgarian official sources render Vientiane as Виентян
Bulgarian geographical transcription emphasizes target-language phonetics and orthography
Lao orthography contains multipart vowel spellings and some vowel spellings vary between open and closed syllables
The orthographic inventory includes 28 composite vowel spellings in the descriptive reference; this is not equivalent to 28 phonemic vowel categories
The spelling ເກິ is documented with pronunciation kɤ
Ueda's description of central Vientiane Lao reports short-long contrasts for the vowel inventory and three diphthongs
The preposed spelling ເ◌ິ represents short /ɤ/ in the descriptive Vientiane-oriented orthography reference
The preposed spelling ເ◌ີ represents long /ɤː/ in the descriptive Vientiane-oriented orthography reference
The spelling ◌ົ represents short /o/ in closed-syllable contexts
The short IA diphthong has spelling variants including ເ◌ັຍ and medial ◌ັຽ
The long IA diphthong has spelling variants including ເ◌ັຽ, ເ◌ຍ, and standalone/medial ◌ຽ in attested contexts
The spelling ເ◌ຶອ represents short /ɯə/
The spelling ເ◌ືອ represents long /ɯːə/
The spelling ◌ົວະ represents short /uə/
The spelling ◌ົວ represents long /uːə/
The preposed spelling ເ◌ົາ represents the /aw/ sequence
The spelling ◌ຳ represents the /am/ sequence
The spellings ◌ໍ and medial ◌ອ represent long /ɔː/ in the contexts described by the reference
The vowel signs ◌ັ and ◌ັອ are used for short vowels in closed-syllable contexts in the descriptive orthography reference
The implemented tone selector is scoped to a Vientiane-oriented five-tone reference matrix; its class/syllable-type/length/mark conditions are not a universal Lao dialect model
The EKI/UNGEGN status report documents the BGN/PCGN 1966 Lao romanization and states that no Lao romanization system has been approved at UN conferences and Laos has no national system
The BGN/PCGN Lao romanization distinguishes syllable-initial and syllable-final consonant spellings and defines a table of vocalic nuclei
The CLDR Lao-Latin transform is marked provisional and explicitly leaves special final-consonant handling as TODO
BGN/PCGN initial spellings kh, th and ph correspond to Lao aspirated consonant letters ຂ/ຄ, ຖ/ທ and ຜ/ພ; h in these digraphs is not an independent /h/ segment
Lao /h/ onsets are represented by ຫ and ຮ, while the phonological inventory distinguishes /h/ from aspirated /kʰ/, /tʰ/ and /pʰ/
The romanization adapter validates onset spellings against the original Lao consonant grapheme and maps aspirated stops with an apostrophe while mapping independent /h/ to Ukrainian г
The CLDR/BGN romanization spelling x corresponds to Lao ຊ, whose Lao consonant value is /s/; it is not the Latin sequence /ks/
The described Lao syllable-coda inventory does not include /h/; a final h is not accepted as a supported Lao coda

The descriptive Lao orthography reference identifies restricted labialized onsets as the productive audible initial-cluster pattern and distinguishes high-class written sequences from independent /h/ clusters
